video_title: Shootaround Media Availability with Caruso & Hartenstein | November 10, 2026 | OKC Thunder

quotes.speaker: Alex Caruso
quotes.summary_phrase: Alex Caruso on the benefits of a long road trip
quotes.excerpt: you get to spend time together, go through the fire together on the road
quotes.quote: Four games is, for NBA standard, not that long of a trip, but for us, I guess it is. So just excited to get back on the road. You get to spend time together, go through the fire together on the road. Just helps build that chemistry together, and it's a little more than playing at home and going to sleep in your own bed.
quotes.social_post: Alex Caruso says the upcoming four game road trip is a good opportunity for the Thunder to build chemistry. He notes that going through the fire together on the road helps the team bond more than playing at home.

structured.context: Alex Caruso discusses the team benefits of going on a four-game road trip.

quotes.speaker: Alex Caruso
quotes.summary_phrase: Alex Caruso on integrating new players into the team
quotes.excerpt: just getting them caught up to speed and being able to maximize their skills
quotes.quote: We are just trying to get the best out of our team. There are the guys that have come in that weren't with us maybe on the first day of training camp. Just getting them caught up to speed and being able to maximize their skills and the talent that they have. There is a reason that they were brought in to be part of the team. So, just trying to do my best to make them feel comfortable and caught up to speed so that they understand how we want to play and the way we go about things.
quotes.social_post: Alex Caruso on integrating new teammates into the Thunder system: We are just trying to get the best out of our team and make sure everyone is caught up to speed so they understand how we want to play.

structured.context: Alex Caruso talks about integrating new players into the team system.

quotes.speaker: Alex Caruso
quotes.summary_phrase: Alex Caruso on the team's defensive intensity
quotes.excerpt: the team that kind of competes more together is going to have the advantage
quotes.quote: It is just a will and grit game where it is like the team that kind of competes more together is going to have the advantage. For us, I think we did a good job of playing together on that end. Defensively is where I am talking about. Just competing, being there to help each other. We are never perfect any night, no team is, but what you do in those moments where you are not perfect to kind of put a band-aid on the mistakes or help each other and cover for each other is where the great teams kind of shine.
quotes.social_post: Alex Caruso on defensive intensity: It is a will and grit game. The team that competes more together is going to have the advantage. We are never perfect, but we shine when we cover for each other.

structured.context: Alex Caruso explains the importance of defensive intensity and team cohesion.

quotes.speaker: Alex Caruso
quotes.summary_phrase: Alex Caruso on the challenge of playing against star players
quotes.excerpt: anytime you play teams with guys that have been All-Stars, there is just the heightened focus
quotes.quote: Anytime you play teams with guys that have been All-Stars, whether it is DeMar DeRozan or Damian Lillard coming back, there is just the heightened focus and attention to detail that you have to have. Anytime you play against great players, that is just kind of what you have to do to show up and try to compete to win. That does not change tonight or the next game or the game after that, but first one on the road, you want to just make sure that you are locked in and tuned into what you need to do.
quotes.social_post: Alex Caruso says playing against stars like DeMar DeRozan or Damian Lillard requires heightened focus and attention to detail. He emphasizes that the team must stay locked in regardless of the opponent.

structured.context: Alex Caruso discusses the heightened focus required when playing against star players.

quotes.speaker: Alex Caruso
quotes.summary_phrase: Alex Caruso on reading the game and being aggressive
quotes.excerpt: it is about being aggressive and then executing when the read is there
quotes.quote: It is about reading the game. It is basketball at the end of the day. For 20 years of my life now, I have been practicing three-on-two transition drills and defensive rotation half-court drills. So at this point, it is pretty ingrained in me what the reads are and what it looks like. It is about being aggressive and then executing when the read is there, whether it is to shoot, pass, or dribble. I enjoy it because it gives me free advantages. It is a lot harder when someone is guarding you one-on-one and they are already in front of you to score in the NBA, but when guys are in rotations and you get to play angles, it makes it a lot easier.
quotes.social_post: Alex Caruso on his basketball IQ: After 20 years of practicing drills, the reads are ingrained in me. It is about being aggressive and executing when the read is there, whether it is to shoot, pass, or dribble.

structured.context: Alex Caruso explains his approach to reading the game and being aggressive on the court.

quotes.speaker: Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.summary_phrase: Isaiah Hartenstein on the team's collective defensive success
quotes.excerpt: when we play as a team, we play as a team offensively and defensively
quotes.quote: I think it is just doing it as a team. I think when we play as a team, we play as a team offensively and defensively, we have a chance to win every night. Again, guys have been stepping up and I think we are just doing it as a unit.
quotes.social_post: Isaiah Hartenstein emphasizes the importance of team play: When we play as a unit offensively and defensively, we have a chance to win every night.

structured.context: Isaiah Hartenstein emphasizes the importance of playing as a unit defensively.

quotes.speaker: Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.summary_phrase: Isaiah Hartenstein on his role as a screener
quotes.excerpt: for me, I am one of the best screeners in the NBA
quotes.quote: Again, just doing my role. I think for me, I am one of the best screeners in the NBA, and so just getting the guys easier looks, getting the guys free. And like I said before, it is just playing as a team. They have been playing, points have been playing good, and so we just want to come in and just establish it from the beginning.
quotes.social_post: Isaiah Hartenstein on his role with the Thunder: I am one of the best screeners in the NBA, so I am just doing my role to get the guys easier looks and get them free.

structured.context: Isaiah Hartenstein describes his role as a screener to help teammates get open looks.

quotes.speaker: Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.summary_phrase: Isaiah Hartenstein on his connection with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.excerpt: he is the best player in the league right now
quotes.quote: It has been good. He is the best player in the league right now, so just making sure, making his life easier. You guys see a lot of different coverages with him, and I think we just, being with him now for a little longer, kind of know what he needs, kind of know what he wants.
quotes.social_post: Isaiah Hartenstein on playing with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander: He is the best player in the league right now. My job is just making sure I make his life easier.

structured.context: Isaiah Hartenstein discusses his developing on-court chemistry with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

quotes.speaker: Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.summary_phrase: Isaiah Hartenstein on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's leadership
quotes.excerpt: all he cares about is winning
quotes.quote: All he cares about is winning, and so I think just being our leader, just coming in, I think he has been doing a good job doing whatever the team needs, us passing, scoring, defending.
quotes.social_post: Isaiah Hartenstein on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander: All he cares about is winning. He has been doing a good job as our leader doing whatever the team needs, whether that is passing, scoring, or defending.

structured.context: Isaiah Hartenstein praises the leadership qualities of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

quotes.speaker: Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.summary_phrase: Isaiah Hartenstein on his development as an off-ball creator
quotes.excerpt: he is so good at just trying to get better and better
quotes.quote: I think he is so good at just trying to get better and better, and I think just little stuff like getting him easier shots, I think it was just with those cuts, it has been big.
quotes.social_post: Isaiah Hartenstein notes that the team is finding success by focusing on small details like off-ball cuts to get easier shots for their playmakers.

structured.context: Isaiah Hartenstein discusses how he is working to create easier scoring opportunities for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

quotes.speaker: Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.summary_phrase: Isaiah Hartenstein on the team's back-to-back schedule
quotes.excerpt: it is another kind of challenge to play a team back-to-back
quotes.quote: I kind of like it. I mean, it is a long flight out here, so you kind of just get them done early. So it is good. I mean, again, it is another kind of challenge to play a team back-to-back, it kind of simulates kind of like a playoff situation, so I think we, we love challenges.
quotes.social_post: Isaiah Hartenstein says he enjoys the challenge of back-to-back games, noting that it simulates a playoff situation and the team loves challenges.

structured.context: Isaiah Hartenstein shares his thoughts on the challenge of playing back-to-back games.

quotes.speaker: Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.summary_phrase: Isaiah Hartenstein on his passing ability
quotes.excerpt: my dad, when I was young, he gave me like a quarter where I could only pass the ball
quotes.quote: I think I told the story before. I mean, my dad, when I was young, he gave me like a quarter where I could only pass the ball. So I kind of started there, and then, especially in the modern NBA, I was, I think it just finding ways to make a difference, and I think just making guys' lives easier with passing was one of those big things.
quotes.social_post: Isaiah Hartenstein reveals the origin of his passing ability: My dad gave me a quarter when I was young where I could only pass the ball. It started there and became a way to make a difference in the modern NBA.

structured.context: Isaiah Hartenstein explains the origin of his passing ability and his focus on making teammates better.
